title: Find the K Tallest Buildings
statement:
You are given the heights of `n` buildings and an integer `k`. Return the heights of the `k` tallest buildings.

Print the `k` heights in **non-increasing** order (tallest first). Buildings with equal heights are separate buildings: if the same height occurs several times it may appear several times in the answer, as many times as it is among the `k` tallest.

**Follow-up:** How would your solution change if the buildings arrive one at a time and you may only keep `k` heights in memory?
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers, the heights of the buildings.
outputFormat: Print `k` integers separated by single spaces: the `k` largest heights in non-increasing order.

examples.explanation: Sorted from tallest, the heights are 45, 45, 30, 12, 9, 7. The two buildings of height 45 are separate buildings, so both are in the top 3, followed by 30.
k equals n, so all buildings are returned, sorted from tallest to shortest.
Only one building is requested, and every building has height 10.

hints: The simplest approach sorts all the heights in descending order and takes the first k. What does it cost?
You do not need the whole order. Keep only the k tallest buildings seen so far.
A min-heap of size k works: push each height, and when the heap grows past k, pop the smallest. Sort the k survivors at the end.
